sec: Medical management · lactulose MOA, rifaximin and liver transplant

items.q: Which pharmacological intervention is designated as the 'most important' treatment for hepatic encephalopathy?
opts: Lactulose bowel wash (4 times a day)
items.exp: Under treatment, Lactulose Bowel wash is explicitly annotated as 'most important' with a frequency of '4 times a day'. (Book p1012)

items.q: What are the recommended dosing options for Rifaximin in the management of hepatic encephalopathy?
opts: 200 mg once daily or 400 mg BD
items.exp: The treatment tree specifies Rifaximin dosing as '400mg TDS / 550 mg BD'. (Book p1012)

items.q: Match each pharmacological agent used in hepatic encephalopathy with its therapeutic description — 1) LOLA 2) Sodium benzoate … A) Promotes non-urea nitrogen clearance by shifting NH3 to ammonium (NH4+) excretion B) L-ornithine L-aspartate, providing substrate for residual urea cycle and glutamine synthesis
items.exp: LOLA (L-ornithine L-aspartate) works alongside branched-chain AAs, while sodium benzoate shifts nitrogen waste via 'NH3 -> NH4+'. (Book p1012)

items.q: Which oral hypoglycemic agent is included among the medical therapies for hepatic encephalopathy on this page?
items.exp: Under the treatment header, the third branch lists 'Acarbose'. (Book p1012)

items.q: Fill up: In the colon, bacterial fermentation of unabsorbed lactulose produces hydrogen gas and ______.
items.exp: The diagram states: 'Lactulose fermented by colonic bacteria to H2 and VFA'. (Book p1012)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the mechanism of action (MOA) of lactulose detailed on this page?
opts: Stimulation of canalicular MRP-2 to accelerate bile salt excretion
Reduction in luminal pH driving conversion of NH3 + H+ -> NH4+ (ammonium trapping)
Formation of volatile fatty acids as preferred substrate for bacteria, reducing ammonia synthesis
Laxative effect promoting rapid excretion of ammonia in stool
items.exp: The three MOA points are ↓ pH (NH3 + H+ -> NH4+), volatile fatty acid formation, and laxative effect; MRP-2 canalicular stimulation is not involved. (Book p1012)

items.q: Why does bacterial consumption of volatile fatty acids (VFA) help reduce ammonia levels in hepatic encephalopathy?
opts: Bacteria utilize VFA as a preferred energy substrate, suppressing their breakdown of amino acids into ammonia
VFA directly binds and neutralizes systemic GABA receptors
VFA accelerates renal glomerular filtration of urea
VFA stimulates hepatic sinusoidal nitric oxide production
items.exp: The flowchart explains: 'Bacteria use VFA as preferred substrate, thus reducing production of ammonia'. (Book p1012)

items.q: Assess the two statements on lactulose: I Lactulose is completely absorbed in the duodenum and jejunum before reaching the colon. II Ionized ammonium (NH4+) formed by luminal acidification cannot easily diffuse back across the colonic mucosa.
items.exp: Statement I is false because lactulose is 'not absorbed in small intestine'. Statement II is true because ionic NH4+ is trapped in the lumen and excreted. (Book p1012)

items.q: What is designated as the 'Last treatment option' for patients with refractory hepatic encephalopathy?
items.exp: The bottom note concludes: 'Liver Transplant : Last treatment option.' (Book p1012)

items.q: A 58-year-old cirrhotic patient with recurrent Grade-II hepatic encephalopathy is managed with lactulose enemas. To further suppress ammoniagenic gut flora without inducing systemic antibiotic toxicity, non-absorbable antibiotic therapy is added. What is the standard drug and oral dosing regimen?
opts: Rifaximin 550 mg BD or 400 mg TDS
Metronidazole 400 mg TDS continuously for 1 year
Neomycin 2 g daily with weekly audiometry
items.exp: The recommended non-absorbable antibiotic is Rifaximin dosed at 550 mg BD or 400 mg TDS. (Book p1012)
